# ClassHierarchy.isA answers false for ancestors above Neo.component.Base

## Welcome 👋

Every Neo class knows its parent, and `Neo.manager.ClassHierarchy.isA(descendant, ancestor)` answers "does this class extend that one?" by walking up that chain. It has a small bug, and fixing it is a good first PR: one method, a failing test first, then the fix.

This is a **good first issue** for Hacktoberfest 2026. It needs Node.js and a clone of this repository: no Docker, no AI setup.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Reserved for first-time Neo.mjs contributors.** The maintainer team will not claim, edit, or implement this issue through **2026-10-31**. Comment here to claim it, and ask anything on this issue.

**Set up once:** follow [Set up the engine from a clone](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md#set-up-the-engine-from-a-clone), including `npm run bundle-browser-deps`: without it the unit suite selects zero tests.

## The bug

`isA()` stops walking as soon as it reaches `Neo.component.Base`, unless the ancestor asked about is `Neo.core.Base`. That shortcut assumed nothing sits between the two. Since then, `Neo.component.Base` extends `Neo.component.Abstract`, so the shortcut now hides a real ancestor. Measured on `dev` (2026-09-23):

| Call | Returns | Should return |
|---|---|---|
| `isA('Neo.button.Base', 'Neo.component.Base')` | `true` | `true` |
| `isA('Neo.button.Base', 'Neo.component.Abstract')` | **`false`** | `true` |
| `isA('Neo.button.Base', 'Neo.core.Base')` | `true` | `true` |

`ClassHierarchy.get('Neo.component.Base').parentClassName` is `'Neo.component.Abstract'`.

## Where things live

- Source: `src/manager/ClassHierarchy.mjs`, method `isA()`
- New test file: `test/playwright/unit/manager/ClassHierarchy.spec.mjs`
- Pattern to copy: `test/playwright/unit/manager/Instance.spec.mjs` (the `setup()` call and imports). Import `src/button/Base.mjs` in the spec so the button classes are registered.

## Done when

- [ ] The spec is written **first** and fails on the `Neo.component.Abstract` case: paste that failing output in your PR.
- [ ] `isA()` no longer stops early at `Neo.component.Base`: the walk ends at `Neo.core.Base` anyway, and the answer cache (`isAQueryMap`) stays.
- [ ] The spec also covers: a class against itself (`true`), a direct parent, an unrelated class (`false`), and a second identical call returning the same answer.
- [ ] `npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/manager/ClassHierarchy.spec.mjs` passes.
- [ ] `npm run test-unit` passes.

## Out of scope

Other `ClassHierarchy` methods, and mixins (they are not in the parent chain).

## While you wait for review

You just pinned one small piece of a multi-threaded application engine: in Neo.mjs your app's code runs inside a web worker, and the main thread only paints. Two things worth ten minutes:

- **See the part nobody expects.** Run `npm run build-themes -- -n -e dev -t all` and `npm run server-start`, open `apps/workstation/`, and drag a tab out of the browser window. It becomes its own OS window, still running, with the same component instances and the same worker. [Benefits: Introduction](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/learn/benefits/Introduction.md) explains why that is possible.
- **Your coding agent can go much further here.** The skills this repository's AI maintainers work with are published on npm as [`neo-agent-skills`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/neo-agent-skills), and they need no Knowledge Base and no Memory Core. With Claude or GPT beside you, the `help wanted` issues are within reach after this one.

- 2026-09-24T12:44:24Z @tobiu referenced in commit `0c83936` - "fix(manager): isA() walks past component.Base to any ancestor (#19130) (#19154)

isA() short-circuited to false as soon as the walk reached Neo.component.Base
and the requested ancestor was not Neo.core.Base. That encoded an assumption
that component.Base extends core.Base directly, which stopped being true once
Neo.component.Abstract was inserted between them: isA('Neo.button.Base',
'Neo.component.Abstract') returned false for every component subclass.

Drop the short-circuit. The loop already ends at Neo.core.Base, so the walk
now sees every class between a descendant and the root, whatever sits there.
The memoization is unchanged.

The new spec pins the parentClassName chain, the ancestor case that used to
fail, a set of non-ancestor cases and the isAQueryMap behaviour."
